All three are tandem arrays of the same ~34-residue TAL-effector repeat; they differ in how many copies each structure contains. SCOPe records this formally with the 're' repeat caveat, which exists precisely so that domains built from different numbers of the same repeating unit can still share one family.

- d2kq5a_ (sunid 264989, '2kq5 A:') -> protein PthA (sunid 267645), species Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. citri [TaxId: 92829]

That is roughly a 15-fold range, so the premise of the question is confirmed from retrieved data.

- The family node a.298.1.1 itself carries a repeat record and a repeat_units entry: description '4cj9 A:259-292', family_sccs a.298.1.1, representative_sid d4cj9a_, representative_sunid 265996. Residues 259-292 of 4cj9 chain A span 34 residues, so SCOPe's canonical repeating unit for this family is a single ~34-residue module.

For d2kq5a_ and d3v6pa_, coordinate_scope is 'canonical_representative' and coordinates_apply_to_requested_node is FALSE. 2. INTERPRETATION

The length difference is a difference in repeat copy number, not a difference in domain identity. A TAL effector central region is modular: one repeat is a short helix-turn-helix-like module, and consecutive modules stack into the elongated superhelical array that SCOPe places in fold a.298. Adding or removing modules changes the length of the array without changing the fold of any module or the packing relationship between neighbors. SCOPe therefore anchors the classification to the common repeating unit, which is why one family absorbs a 51-residue record and a 752-residue record.

Using the retrieved 34-residue unit, simple arithmetic puts d2kq5a_ at about 1.5 units, d3v6pa_ at roughly 11 units, and d4cj9a_ at roughly 22 units plus terminal capping sequence. Treat those counts as my arithmetic inference from retrieved lengths, NOT as retrieved SCOPe values: SCOPe returned no per-domain repeat count and no repeat boundaries for d2kq5a_ or d3v6pa_. The 'single repeat' comment on d2kq5a_ is retrieved and does independently confirm that this entry represents a minimal, roughly one-module excerpt rather than a full array.

The 're' code is the key to the apparent paradox. It is not a complaint that the classification is wrong. It is the curators' mechanism for flagging that family members legitimately contain different numbers of the same small repeating unit, so that sequence length and residue-count mismatch between members must not be read as evidence against shared family membership.

- Shared FAMILY a.298.1.1 is the deepest shared level here and is the strongest statement SCOPe makes. It indicates a close relationship and clear common ancestry of the repeat module across PthA, dHax3, and BurrH, despite BurrH coming from a different genus.
- Shared SUPERFAMILY a.298.1 would support probable common ancestry on its own, but it adds no discrimination beyond the family in this case because all three are already in the same family.
- Shared FOLD a.298 carries unusually little information here. The retrieved children of fold 267589 are a single superfamily, a.298.1, with has_more false. Fold and superfamily membership are coextensive in this release, so 'same fold' here cannot be offered as independent corroboration of homology. Shared fold in general indicates structural similarity only and does not by itself establish common ancestry.
- Shared CLASS a is only a gross secondary-structure statement and is not evolutionary evidence.
- Protein nodes (PthA, dHax3, BurrH) and species nodes are SCOPe hierarchy levels. They are not external taxonomy or sequence-database records and should not be cited as such.

- No DNA-specificity transfer. Family membership does NOT mean these three bind the same DNA target. TAL repeat specificity is set by variable residues within each module and by the module order along the array, so arrays of different length and different module composition read different sequences. SCOPe's family assignment says nothing about target site, affinity, or which bases are recognized. The repeat-variable-residue mechanism itself is general background from pretrained knowledge and was not retrieved from any SCOPe response in this task.
- No function or activity transfer. dHax3 is a designed/engineered TAL-type protein and BurrH is from a different genus than the two Xanthomonas entries. Shared family does not make their biological roles, host interactions, or in-vivo activities equivalent. The question of why these particular proteins were grouped together, in terms of the sequence or structural analysis the curators performed, was not verified: the xrefs sections for all three domains returned empty uniprot, pfam, pubmed, and species lists, so no supporting literature was retrieved.
- No template interchangeability. A 51-residue, single-repeat record cannot substitute for a 752-residue superhelical array as a modeling template, and the reverse substitution discards the array context. Shared family placement is not a statement that members are interchangeable structural templates.
- No quality ranking. I retrieved no SPACI, AEROSPACI, resolution, or R-factor records for 2kq5, 3v6p, or 4cj9, so I make no claim about which is the better structure. Note separately that d4cj9a_ being the repeat-coordinate representative is a coordinate reference for the 34-residue unit, not a finding that it is the best-quality or best structural representative of the family.
